clue.text: What comes after I imitate mockery

parts.note: in the alphabet the letter following I is J
to ape someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: Someone owns up that what follows their impression of another person is pure ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the letter, and the thing after it in the alphabet is J.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a joke or prank played at someone's expense, a form of teasing ridicule.

clue.text: Money for nothing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: American slang for cash
second meaning: as in 'you don't know ...', not a thing

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads like the Dire Straits song title, but 'for' only joins two separate senses of one slang word.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang the word means cash, and also, as in 'jack squat', nothing whatsoever.

clue.text: Plan initially devised to create a pattern

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word plan is wanted here

parts.note: plans that are laid are devised or arranged

explanation.surface: A scheme is first worked out in order to make a design.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a tartan, a criss-cross pattern of coloured stripes on cloth.

clue.text: In the absence of objective fact, send leader of team ahead of Yankee slugger

definitions.text: In the absence of objective fact

indicators.note: places the team letter in front of the slugger's name

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so team gives its first

parts.note: Babe Ruth, the New York Yankees' great home-run hitter

explanation.surface: A manager ships the captain off ahead of a baseball star, with no facts to back the decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe Ruth was the New York Yankees' famous home-run hitter of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-truth describes a climate where emotion and belief count for more than objective evidence; it was Oxford's 2016 word of the year.

clue.text: Place outside of Tripoli for naked babies

parts.note: to place something is to put it

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A spot on the edge of the Libyan capital set aside for unclothed infants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun, a location near Tripoli, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Putti are the chubby nude cherubs of Renaissance and Baroque painting and sculpture.

clue.text: Doctors eating a piece of tasty fish

indicators.note: the doctors take the tasty letter inside them
a small piece of the word tasty, its first letter

explanation.surface: Medics tuck into a portion of delicious seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' could be a verb meaning tampers, but here it is plural doctors that do the eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeons are large primitive bony fishes, prized as the source of caviar.

clue.text: Badly want family-friendly sound from a banjo

indicators.note: the word want is done badly, its letters set in a different order

parts.note: G is the American film rating for general audiences, suitable for all the family

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a wholesome tune plucked on a banjo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly want' reads as a phrase meaning crave; 'badly' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the sharp ringing note of a plucked string, typical of the banjo.

clue.text: Bearing one child at a time, finally, you almost get excited about small quantity of liquor

definitions.text: Bearing one child at a time

indicators.note: the final letter of the word you is wanted

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped, leaving the word almost complete

parts.note: to arouse is to stir up or excite

explanation.surface: A mother of single babies is told she will get worked up over a little drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only links the pieces here.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniparous is the zoological term for animals that normally produce a single offspring per birth.

clue.text: Some deaths ravaged family dwellings

indicators.note: the words some deaths are wrecked and their letters reordered

explanation.surface: Several fatalities have devastated houses where families live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like it is picking out a hidden word, but both words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A homestead is a house with its land, typically a farm home occupied by a family.

clue.text: Talking software in Panama, for instance, and beginning to babble in bed

indicators.note: the hat and the babble letter go inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a Panama is a kind of straw hat

indicators.note: the beginning of the word babble, its first letter

explanation.surface: Speech software in the Central American country, and a toddler starting to burble in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama is a hat, not the country; the 'for instance' marks it as an example of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatbot is a computer program that holds conversations with people, typically by text.

clue.text: Pick up rock and toss jacket

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the pieces up means they read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to lob is to throw high

explanation.surface: Grab a stone and fling your coat off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' looks like an instruction to lift the rock, but it turns the pieces upside down in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket ending above the waist, of Spanish origin.

clue.text: Rotate front of skull 90 degrees with radioactive element

indicators.note: the opening letter of the skull word is turned on its side
the letter at the front of the word for skull is the one changed
a quarter turn of that curved front letter makes it look like a different letter

parts.note: the cranium is the part of the skull enclosing the brain

explanation.surface: An instruction to tip the face of a skull sideways next to something giving off radiation.
explanation.walkthrough: A visual trick: write a C, turn it through a right angle, and it becomes a U.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is the heavy metallic element whose isotopes fuel nuclear reactors and weapons.

clue.text: Monstrous giant taking on most of tedious, mature behavior

indicators.note: the rearranged giant takes the dull letters inside it
the word giant is made monstrous, its letters misshapen into a new order
all but the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: A hideous ogre takes on the dreary business of acting like a grown-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monstrous giant' paints a single ogre, but 'Monstrous' is the instruction and 'giant' its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Adulting is the jokey modern verb-noun for doing the dull chores expected of a grown-up, a 2016 Oxford shortlist word.

clue.text: Philip and Jimmy (two musicians) in a precipitous position for women and minorities

definitions.text: a precipitous position for women and minorities

parts.note: Philip Glass, the American minimalist composer
Jimmy Cliff, the Jamaican reggae singer

explanation.surface: Two musicians are stuck on a dangerous ledge reserved for women and minorities.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'two musicians' tells you to read the first names as famous surnames.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names how women and minority leaders are often promoted during crises, so their position is precarious and likely to fail.

clue.text: A South American capital beginning to comfort green, inexperienced actress

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: the beginnings of both comfort and green, their first letters

parts.note: someone raw is untried or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A Peruvian city starts to reassure a nervous young performer making her debut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green, inexperienced actress' reads as one description; 'green' only gives its first letter, and 'actress' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali MacGraw is the American film star of Love Story and The Getaway.

clue.text: Group of workers left a foot deformity lined with gold

indicators.note: the gold goes inside the foot deformity like a lining

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling at the base of the big toe

explanation.surface: A misshapen foot left with a gold lining, the kind of thing that might befall a trade worker.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A labor union is the American term for a trade union, an organized association of employees.

clue.text: Porter, e.g., accommodating ruler in Rome, Italy — briefly an advocate of separation from Europe

definitions.text: an advocate of separation from Europe

indicators.note: the beer holds the ruler and the shortened Italy inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark style of beer

indicators.note: the name Italy is cut short to its opening letters

explanation.surface: A doorman, say, puts up a Roman king in Italy, briefly a campaigner for leaving Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a doorman or Cole Porter; it is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brexiteer is a supporter of Britain's withdrawal from the European Union, the cause won in the 2016 referendum.

clue.text: Vermin allegedly from Scandinavia — or carried by returning sailor (what a bore)

indicators.note: the word or is carried inside the other letters
the sailor and the bore are read backwards together

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Rats said to come from Norway, or brought by a sailor coming home who is deadly dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allegedly' is fair: despite the name, the brown rat spread from Asia, not Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norway rat is the common brown rat, a pest found in cities worldwide.

clue.text: You and I getting approval for being aware of social injustice

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for the adjective, alert to injustice

indicators.note: the pair receives the approval letters inside it

parts.note: together you and I are we
an OK is a go-ahead or approval

explanation.surface: The two of us win endorsement for our social conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: Woke is American slang, from African American usage, for being alert to racial and social injustice.

clue.text: Hispanic of any gender is careless to swallow metal

indicators.note: the careless word takes the metal down inside it

explanation.surface: A sloppy Latino of any gender is so careless as to gulp down a bit of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Latinx is the gender-neutral term coined in the US for people of Latin American heritage, a 2016 Oxford shortlist word.

clue.text: Proper athletic event

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fitting or suitable, an old adjective
second meaning: a sports competition such as a track ...

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a properly run sports day, but the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means fitting or right; as a noun it is an American sports contest.

clue.text: Entered illegally, with locks broken by personal assistants

indicators.note: the locks word is split open and the assistants placed in the gap

parts.note: tresses are locks of hair; tressed is the hair-arranging verb
PA is the abbreviation for personal assistant

explanation.surface: Intruders got in by having their aides break the locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like door locks; it is hair, read as the verb for arranging it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trespass is to go on to land or property without permission.

clue.text: See 12
Chip: fit or out of shape?

indicators.note: the letters of fit or are bent into a different form

explanation.surface: Asking whether a crisp is healthy or fattening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit or out of shape' reads as a fitness question; 'fit or' supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fritos are an American brand of corn chips, so one piece is a single chip.

clue.text: Racist movement sounds totally unoriginal

indicators.note: the phrase for totally unoriginal is said out loud to give the answer's sound

explanation.surface: A bigoted political movement is dismissed as entirely derivative.
explanation.definitionFit: The alt-right is the far-right American movement promoting white nationalism, prominent in 2016.

clue.text: At first, throw a garden tool in the lake

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word throw is used

parts.note: a hoe is a long-handled weeding tool

explanation.surface: Someone begins by chucking a gardening implement into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is the large alpine lake on the California-Nevada border.

clue.text: In Denmark, a cozy quality (like a soufflé) rises after hours

indicators.note: the soufflé letters come after the hours letter
in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: a soufflé is made of eggs, so it is eggy

explanation.surface: A Danish sense of comfort, light as a soufflé that puffs up late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' looks like the soufflé puffing up in the oven, but it reverses the letters in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hygge is the Danish idea of warm, convivial cosiness and contentment.

clue.text: Called up to growl

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for called is read from the bottom up

explanation.surface: Someone was summoned in order to snarl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Called up' reads as phoned or drafted; 'up' turns the letters around in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnar is an old word meaning to snarl, the sound an angry dog makes.

clue.text: Dancer, perhaps stepping back, missing violin finale and sounding more like an oboe

indicators.note: the remaining letters walk backwards, read right to left
the violin letter is lost from the reindeer

parts.note: Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

indicators.note: the finale of the word violin is its last letter

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer retreats from a violin's closing bars to an oboe-like tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancer' is the reindeer from 'The Night Before Christmas', not a ballerina.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a reed instrument, so a reedier tone is thinner and more nasal, closer to its sound.

clue.text: Former Attorney General invested in sweetheart's idea for a massive Defense Department expansion?

definitions.text: idea for a massive Defense Department expansion?
definitions.note: a noun phrase for the noun answer: a six-sided Pentagon

indicators.note: the former attorney general is placed inside the sweetheart

parts.note: hon, short for honey, a term of endearment

explanation.surface: An ex-attorney general backs a lover's scheme to grow the military massively.
explanation.walkthrough: The Defense Department is housed in the Pentagon; add a side and five becomes six, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A hexagon has six sides, one more than the five-sided Pentagon building.

clue.text: "Fight back frequently!"—cry for attention contained in valuable 2016 honorific awarded by the editors of the Oxford Dictionaries to one of nine finalists in the completed grid

definitions.text: 2016 honorific awarded by the editors of the Oxford Dictionaries to one of nine finalists in the completed grid

indicators.note: the fight word is read backwards
the frequent and the cry go inside the valuable word

parts.note: oft is an old word for often
hey is a shout to get notice

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome shout sits within a description of Oxford's annual language prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine of the ten 2016 shortlist words are in the grid; POST-TRUTH won the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford Dictionaries names one term each year as its word of the year, the coinage that best captures it.

clue.text: See 29
